answer.label: confirmed
answer.reason: Confirmed for a fresh household-enabled standalone administration panel with stable active authorization, preferences.read granted, and preferences.write denied. This is a supported configuration. The backend returns the owner's saved preferences and the controller loads them, but controls.preferences requires write authority. The preferences button is therefore disabled, and its handler independently returns before adding a draft. Because preference details are only rendered through drafts, the user cannot inspect saved preference choices, particularly the routine-participation-summary setting. This is a presentation read-access failure, not a failed GET. Automatic locale application and previously opened readable drafts limit the finding but do not resolve the fresh-panel route.

premises.claim: A valid configuration can retain preferences.read while denying preferences.write. Both are ordinary permissions; preference writes are not protected from exceptions, and matching member exceptions override default grants.

findings.title: Keep saved preferences readable without write access
findings.description: Saved preferences are accessible only through this edit button. When preferences.read is granted but preferences.write is denied, or a read-only outage lease applies, the button is disabled and no current preference values are rendered elsewhere. A participant opening the workspace cannot inspect their saved routine-summary setting despite having authorized, successfully loaded preference data.
findings.evidence: AdministrationController.load() fetches preferences under preferences.read independently of preferences.write. Its controls.preferences requires full write access and administrationAllowed(), which checks preferences.write. render() provides only the write-gated opener, while fields() and summary() expose preference values only for an existing draft. open() also rejects disabled controls. Thus a fresh read-authorized, write-denied view has no path to the loaded values, violating the documented preservation of permitted local reads.
findings.suggestion: Render a read-only summary whenever view.preferences is available, independently of controls.preferences. Keep mutation controls governed by the existing write checks.

findings.title: Allow retained drafts to be corrected after definitive rejection
findings.description: After Save changes, draft.sent remains true permanently. A definitive server rejection therefore leaves both Save changes and Back to editing disabled, even after current write controls become available again. Users cannot correct the retained draft. Resetting or closing and reopening replaces their entered values with current server data.
findings.evidence: A household name change with time_zone='Not/AZone' passes administrationCommand's text validation and reaches backend timezone validation, which rejects it as invalid_time_zone. HttpAdministrationServer maps HTTP 422 to a rejected outcome, and AdministrationController records a terminal rejected journal entry. That entry permits editing again, but save() previously set draft.sent=true. No outcome handler clears that flag. The changed Back button consequently remains disabled. reset() calls open(), rebuilding the payload from server facts and losing the entered name.
findings.suggestion: Associate submission outcomes with their drafts and restore an editable continuation after a definitive rejection or before-send failure. Retain entered values, require review again, and preserve immutable journal records and unresolved-request locks.
